// BranchDeleteRemote deletes a branch from the remote repository.
//
// The request must not follow redirects: Go rewrites a DELETE into a GET when it follows a
// 301/302/303, so a redirected delete would report success while having deleted nothing. GitHub
// answers with a redirect when the owner or name in the path differs in case from the canonical
// repository, so rather than following it we reissue the DELETE against the location it points to.
func BranchDeleteRemote(client *Client, repo ghrepo.Interface, branch string) error {
	path, err := safeurl.JoinPath("repos", repo.RepoOwner(), repo.RepoName(), "git", "refs", fmt.Sprintf("heads/%s", branch))
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	resp, err := client.Request(repo.RepoHost(), http.MethodDelete, path.String(), nil, WithoutFollowingRedirects())
	if err != nil {
		location, ok := redirectLocation(err)
		if !ok {
			return err
		}
		resp, err = client.Request(repo.RepoHost(), http.MethodDelete, location, nil, WithoutFollowingRedirects())
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()

	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusNoContent {
		return UnexpectedStatusError(resp)
	}

	return nil
}

// redirectLocation reports the target of a redirect that was surfaced as an error by a request
// made with WithoutFollowingRedirects.
func redirectLocation(err error) (string, bool) {
	var httpErr HTTPError
	if !errors.As(err, &httpErr) {
		return "", false
	}
	if httpErr.StatusCode < 300 || httpErr.StatusCode > 399 || httpErr.Headers == nil {
		return "", false
	}
	location := httpErr.Headers.Get("Location")
	if location == "" {
		return "", false
	}
	return location, true
}
